overview: Four workstreams, ordered D → A → B → C per the brief's own priority (cursor bug + onboarding reliability first, installer next, phone last), maximizing parallelism inside that order via a dependency DAG (8 waves below). Every critique's BLOCKING finding is fixed in the plan; MISSING items are folded into the owning task's brief; CROSS_CONFLICTS are resolved by explicit sequencing (not parallel worktrees on the same function) — the two most dangerous ones: (1) migrate_v12 is owned EXCLUSIVELY by A5 (adds `machines.addresses`); C8's four daemon columns land as migrate_v13, built on top of A5. (2) tosse-code's `run_actor` FdDetach handling is refactored ONCE into a pure `reconnect_policy_for_reason` table by D2 (landing first); A2's "daemon_missing" reason and B/C's later work are just table entries added on top, never a second hand-edit of the match. flightdeck-server's `attach.rs`/`session.rs` are touched by D1 first, then B1 (tiny, version field only), then C1-C3 last — sequenced, not concurrent. Genuinely broken designs from the critiques are corrected, not just re-specified: B's SUDO_ASKPASS (can't run a Mac-local helper on the remote host) is replaced with piping the captured password to `sudo -S` over the same already-open SSH stdin; B's BatchMode=yes vs SSH_ASKPASS contradiction is resolved with a dedicated non-batch bootstrap SSH call (SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force); B's config.json race gets a real cross-process file lock, not an in-process mutex that can't span the separate `flightdeckd init` CLI process; C's relay POST /nodes gets its OWN rate limiter instead of poisoning the shared WS auth throttle on legitimate empty polls; C's regenerate-pairing flow now actually revokes the old token everywhere (today it's a silent no-op, verified); D's replay-compaction (fd_skip) is deliberately parked, built but permanently dead-switched-off, until A1's daemon-version probe exists to gate it safely. flightdeck-server is confirmed on Armand's PERSONAL `clousty8` GitHub account — B's private-binary-distribution design inherits the same bus-factor problem it explicitly rejected in the public-repo alternative; flagged as a real decision, not silently accepted. Estimated total: ~4 weeks D+A core reliability, ~2.5 weeks B installer, ~2 weeks C phone — with A/D/most of B parallelizable across 2-3 concurrent worktrees/conversations.

tasks.title: Bounded attach write-timeout + fd_detach{stalled}
tasks.brief: Root cause of the cursor incident: attach.rs::handle_conn's writer (~146-161) does an unbounded write_all/flush to the attach client's socket, so a degraded-but-alive link blocks the write forever — self.attached stays Some, the daemon queues every new line, no fd_detach is ever sent, and byte-budget CLIENT_QUEUE_BYTES_MAX (128MiB) never trips on small stream_event deltas. Add `pub(crate) const ATTACH_WRITE_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(20)` near CLIENT_QUEUE_BYTES_MAX/RING_BYTES_MAX in session.rs. Wrap the writer's write_all/flush in `tokio::time::timeout(ATTACH_WRITE_TIMEOUT, ...)`. On timeout: best-effort ONE short (2s) write of `frames::fd_detach("stalled", None)` (skip on a hard non-timeout write error — pipe's already gone), then break exactly as today's error path does — this naturally nulls self.attached via the actor's next push() failing, zero session.rs state-machine changes needed. Add `fd_skip`-adjacent doc: extend fd_detach's reason doc comment in frames.rs to document "stalled" = daemon gave up on a non-responsive write, session still alive, client should reconnect — and update tosse-code's mirrored FdDetachMsg doc comment (protocol.rs) in the SAME PR/commit since they're a matched pair (do this half here even though the Rust enum is in tosse-code — a one-line comment edit, list it as a note for whoever lands D2). Do NOT modify the client-facing wire shape of fd_detach itself.
tests: Unit: tokio::net::UnixStream::pair() — feed the writer-task logic one end, never read the other, assert the write attempt errors/gives up within ATTACH_WRITE_TIMEOUT+slack instead of hanging (deterministic, no ssh/daemon/network, non-ignored).
Unit: fd_detach("stalled", None) shape round-trips; is_replayable_line(fd_skip-adjacent stalled frame)==false already true by construction, add an explicit assertion.
Existing client_queue_kills_stalled_clients and other session.rs tests remain green unmodified.
acceptance: A daemon-side attach write that cannot complete within 20s causes the daemon to give up on that client within one timeout window and best-effort send fd_detach{reason:"stalled"}.
No change to behavior for any write that completes normally.

tasks.title: tosse-code: reconnect-policy refactor + reader_loop parse-order fix
tasks.brief: Two independent, bundled fixes in src-tauri/src/supervisor/session.rs and transport.rs. (1) Extract run_actor's inline FdDetach reason handling (session.rs ~576-619, the `match d.reason.as_str() {...}` plus the unconditional `no_reconnect = Some(d.reason)`) into a pure, unit-testable `fn reconnect_policy_for_reason(reason: &str) -> (Option<String> /*notice message*/, bool /*terminal — stop reconnecting*/)`. Table: "exited"->(Some(msg),true), "replaced"->(Some("Another client took over this remote session."),true), "stopped"->(None,true), "stalled"->(Some("Connection stalled — reconnecting…"),false), everything else incl. today's "error"->(Some(msg),true) — i.e. ONLY "stalled" is reconnect-eligible; every other/unknown reason keeps EXACT current terminal behavior. This table is the shared extension point later tasks (A2's "daemon_missing") add ONE line to, never a second hand-edit of run_actor's match. Wire it into run_actor exactly where the old inline match was. (2) reader_loop (transport.rs ~824-841) currently does `lines_seen.fetch_add(1,...)` for any is_replayable_line(trimmed) line BEFORE attempting `serde_json::from_str::<CliMessage>` — a replayable-typed line that fails to parse is silently counted as delivered but never actually forwarded/rendered, permanently lost (never replayed). Move the increment inside the `Ok(msg) => {...}` success arm only.
tests: Table-driven unit test over reconnect_policy_for_reason: all 4 named reasons + one unknown reason, asserting exact (message, terminal) pairs — the direct regression test for 'stalled' becoming the first non-terminal reason.
transport.rs unit (tokio::io::duplex(), feed two lines: one well-formed replayable + one replayable-typed-but-malformed): assert lines_seen==1 not 2, no process spawn needed.
acceptance: FdDetach{reason:"stalled"} does not stop the actor's reconnect loop; every other current reason (exited/replaced/stopped/error) is byte-for-byte unchanged.
A replayable-typed line that fails to deserialize is not counted toward lines_seen and is therefore replayed on next reconnect instead of lost.

tasks.title: [PARKED — decision-gated] flightdeck-server: fd_skip replay compaction (dead-off by default)
tasks.brief: Bandwidth optimization, built but never wired live until A1's daemon-version probe exists (see decision). Add `supports_skip: bool` to AttachReq/attach's on_attach signature (session.rs ~840-881): when true, replay via a NEW pure `fn compact_replay(ring: &[(u64,String)], effective_from: u64) -> Vec<ReplayLine>` (ReplayLine = Line(u64,String) | Skip(u64)); when false (default, every current client), byte-for-byte identical to today. Algorithm: walk the ring tracking open stream_event spans keyed by parent_tool_use_id; forward message_start and content_block_start lines always (needed for tool_use id/name + the assembler's Skill-arm timing — never compact these); for a CLOSED span (message_stop seen at some LATER point in the ring, i.e. NOT the trailing still-open span at ring end), buffer content_block_delta/content_block_stop/message_delta/message_stop into ONE fd_skip(K) instead of forwarding them; a TRAILING open span (client joining mid-turn) is forwarded fully uncompacted, always. CRITICAL fix over the original design (flagged blocking by review): K must count ONLY elided lines with seq > effective_from, never the whole span — otherwise a reattach landing inside an already-partially-delivered closed span inflates the client's credited lines_seen past the daemon's true seq, and on_attach's `req.cursor.min(self.seq)` silently clamps it down on the NEXT reattach, causing a permanent silent gap (the exact bug class this workstream exists to fix). Add `pub fn fd_skip(lines: u64) -> String` to frames.rs. Add `--supports-skip` flag to `flightdeckd attach` CLI (main.rs) and `AttachParams.supports_skip` (attach.rs), but nothing in this task calls it with true — it lands fully inert.

tasks.title: probe_remote: flightdeckd presence+version check, combined with the claude check
tasks.brief: src-tauri/src/ipc/commands.rs::probe_remote (~3315-3359) today runs ONE ssh round-trip: `command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 && claude --version || { echo FLIGHTDECK_NO_CLAUDE >&2; exit 3; }`. tasks.title: run_actor: fast-fail when the remote daemon binary is missing
tasks.brief: Today, if flightdeckd simply isn't on PATH, run_actor's remote reconnect loop retries FOREVER on one generic 'Connection to the server lost — reconnecting…' notice (no FdDetach is ever produced by a spawn failure, so the existing exit check never fires). decisions_for_user.question: MIN_DAEMON_VERSION policy: flightdeckd has no versioning/bump discipline yet against tosse-code. Ship the version comparator as dormant scaffolding (always passes until someone deliberately bumps it) or defer the 'outdated' half entirely until B's installer exists?
options: Ship as dormant scaffolding now (A1's default)
Defer 'outdated' check until B ships an update mechanism
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Ship as dormant scaffolding — costs nothing, degrades safely, and is already wired for when versioning discipline starts.

decisions_for_user.question: Should a MISSING flightdeckd hard-block pairing entirely (consistent with today's missing-claude behavior), or should pairing succeed with a persistent warning, since no in-app installer exists until B ships?
options: Allow pairing with a persistent warning
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Hard-block — consistent with existing behavior; revisit once B's installer can actually fix the gap in-app.

decisions_for_user.question: Should the bootstrap discover a 'public' address candidate via a 3rd-party 'what's my IP' service (adds a new external dependency + reveals the server's public IP to that service), or stay manual-entry-only?
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Manual-entry-only — matches the repo's own privacy-conscious precedent (tosseClientFavicons OFF by default).

decisions_for_user.question: Should the discovered/candidate address list be visible and editable in Settings, or stay fully automatic and invisible?
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Ship invisible first; add visibility as a follow-up if it turns out to matter in practice.

decisions_for_user.question: A2 deliberately leaves 'retry forever, one generic notice' unchanged for every ambiguous failure except exit-127 'flightdeckd: command not found'. Should that broader behavior also change (give up after N attempts with a clearer persistent banner)?
options: Also add a give-up-after-N policy for ambiguous failures
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Leave unchanged — this is a separate, later decision; A2's narrow fix already closes the one unambiguous case.

decisions_for_user.question: Should the orphan ssh_keys/ sweep (A7) be automated, or is a manual one-off cleanup on your machine preferred?
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Automate — the grace window makes it low-risk and it prevents recurrence.

decisions_for_user.question: D's fd_skip bandwidth-compaction optimization (D5/D6): build it now but permanently dead-switched-off until A1's version probe gates it, or drop it from this program entirely?
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Build now, dead-gated — the boundary-condition bug the review found is now fixed, and it's ready the moment A1 lands, at zero live risk in the meantime.

decisions_for_user.question: Should a user-facing 'reconnecting, catching up…' notice appear during a multi-minute silent gap (today shows nothing until a message arrives or hard disconnect)?
options: Ship D1-D4 with no new UI (current plan)
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Skip for now — D1-D4 is a reliability fix, not a UX change; revisit if real-world stalls prove disruptive.

decisions_for_user.question: Should a Mac-side proactive staleness watchdog (reconnect sooner than SSH's own ~15s keepalive on literally zero bytes, not just zero replayable lines) be built? Investigation suggests fd_detach{stalled} may rarely reach the Mac in the real bandwidth-limited failure mode.
options: Rely on D1-D4 alone for now
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Defer — observe D1-D4 in production first; this is a real behavior/timing change needing its own threshold decision.

decisions_for_user.question: Sleep-masking (B9): opt-out checkbox (default ON) vs always-on/non-negotiable? And should it apply to root-owned servers too, or only non-root+linger boxes?
options: Opt-out checkbox, default ON, applies to root too (B9's default)
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Opt-out checkbox default ON, applied uniformly including root — it's a real machine-level behavior change per the repo's own reversibility principle, and sleep-masking is unrelated to linger (which root doesn't need).

decisions_for_user.question: Private SSH key custody: keep today's plain 0600 file (the ssh binary needs a file path via -i regardless) or move into Keychain like mac_token — bigger change, revisit later?
options: Keep plain 0600 file for v1 (B7's default)
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Keep as-is for v1; Keychain would still require writing a temp file per connection since ssh -i needs a path.

decisions_for_user.question: Host-key fingerprint on first connect: show for transparency only, non-blocking (B7's default), or require an explicit 'yes, this matches' confirmation click?
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Non-blocking for v1 — lowest first-run friction; can be hardened later if needed.

decisions_for_user.question: Decoupled daemon-update channel (fetch a newer flightdeckd independent of a Mac app release): build now, or ship v1's 'update' repair action as 'just re-push whatever binary is bundled in the currently-installed Mac app'?
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Defer — avoids adding new GitHub auth surface on the Mac; the simple re-push covers the common case.

decisions_for_user.question: flightdeck-server is confirmed to live on YOUR personal GitHub account (clousty8), private. B's binary-distribution design fetches release assets from it via a fine-grained PAT into tosse-code's release.yml — who owns/rotates that PAT, and should the repo move to an org/bot account first, given this is the exact bus-factor problem B's own design explicitly rejected when it ruled out a public repo?
options: Move flightdeck-server to an org/bot-owned account or a scoped GitHub App/deploy key before wiring the PAT
Use a PAT on your personal account for now, revisit later
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Move ownership (or at minimum use a scoped deploy key/GitHub App, not a personal PAT) before wiring it into a release pipeline that only Alexandre can trigger — this is a real governance gap, not just a preference.

decisions_for_user.question: Passwordless-sudo-unavailable fallback (B9): is a second native 'sudo password' prompt on first run acceptable, or should the wizard hard-require passwordless sudo be pre-configured and fail with copy-paste instructions otherwise?
options: Second native prompt as fallback (B9's default)
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Second native prompt — lower friction for a first-run wizard; the copy-paste fallback still exists for anyone who prefers it.

decisions_for_user.question: Per-machine macOS Keychain UX: B11's fix consolidates every server's mac_token into ONE shared Keychain item (one first-access prompt total) instead of N items for N servers — confirm this is the right default versus N separate items (which would trigger N separate permission prompts, unlike every other feature's one-item-per-feature precedent in this app)?
options: One shared Keychain item for all servers (B11's default)
decisions_for_user.recommendation: One shared item — matches the repo's existing one-item-per-feature Keychain precedent and avoids a prompt storm as servers are added.

decisions_for_user.question: What should the Mac's own relay-node label default to in the phone's node list: a fixed generic string, the machine's hostname, or a free-text Settings field?
options: Fixed default 'This Mac', still editable (C11's default)
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Fixed default 'This Mac' with the field editable — simple by default, flexible if wanted.

decisions_for_user.question: When the phone scans a SECOND, unrelated pairing link (different Mac/account, different phoneToken): should it ADD that as another independent pairing group, or REPLACE the existing pairing as today?
options: Add as a new independent pairing group (C12a's assumption)
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Add — least surprising now that multi-node pairing is the normal case; replacing would be a silent, surprising loss of access.

decisions_for_user.question: Should 'Unpair this phone' stay all-or-nothing (forgets every node under every pairing group), or should Settings gain a way to remove ONE node while keeping the rest? The former needs no new UI; the latter is real additional scope. Relatedly: should local unpair also proactively revoke server-side, or is 'forget locally, Mac separately manages revocation' (C10's approach) acceptable for v1?
options: All-or-nothing unpair, local-only (C12c's default), server-side revocation handled separately by C10's Mac-initiated paths
Add per-node unpair + have local unpair also revoke server-side
decisions_for_user.recommendation: All-or-nothing + local-only for v1 — C10 already fixes the one genuinely broken revocation path (regenerate-pairing); per-node unpair is clean future scope, not required now.

decisions_for_user.question: When a conversation has both a Mac-set name and a daemon-side ai-title (e.g. phone-started, never opened on the Mac) — should the Mac's push always win once it has ever sent a non-empty title, or should ai-title be allowed to fill in when the Mac genuinely has none yet?
options: Mac always wins once set (C1/C9's default, matches set_title_authoritative's design)
Allow ai-title to fill when Mac has none
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Mac always wins — matches the already-chosen set_title_authoritative semantics (unconditional overwrite), keep it consistent.

decisions_for_user.question: Does phone multi-target need its own Settings toggle separate from the existing remote-control enable switch, or is it implicitly covered by turning remote control on at all?
decisions_for_user.recommendation: No new toggle — an unpaired server is unreachable regardless, a second switch would be redundant.

risks: tosse-code's run_actor remote-reconnect loop (session.rs) is edited in sequence by D2 (refactor into a pure reconnect_policy_for_reason table), A2 (adds 'daemon_missing'), and A6 (adds address rotation) — sequencing via depends_on avoids concurrent edits, but this remains the single highest-review-risk region in the codebase per the repo's own admission (one ignored, thinly-covered live test today); each landing still deserves careful review against the two that came before it.

flightdeck-server's attach.rs/session.rs/main.rs are touched by D1 (write-timeout), B1 (version field, tiny), and C1-C3 (phone-token primitives) — sequenced D→B→C by wave, not concurrent, but a real rebase is still expected for whoever lands C1 last.

B0's musl cross-compile spike is unverified today (no cross/musl toolchain, only Docker) and gates the ENTIRE binary-distribution half of workstream B (B2 onward) — if ring's asm fails on aarch64-musl, a fallback (different crypto provider, or dropping aarch64 support) must be chosen before B2 can proceed.

B10's claude non-interactive/device-flow login invocation is unverified and coupled to the CLI's current UX — a future claude CLI upgrade could silently break claude_login's scraping; flagged as a recurring manual verification item, not a one-time fix.

D's own investigation found the fd_detach{stalled} best-effort notice writes over the SAME potentially-stalled local pipe that caused the original write to time out — in the real bandwidth-limited (not frozen-process) failure mode, it may rarely be delivered before the Mac's own hard disconnect fires anyway. D1-D4 are still a net improvement (they remove a provably-unbounded blocking path) even if the notification path underperforms in that specific scenario.

D's investigation found a SECOND, unremarked recurrence of the same under-delivery pattern on josty-cc immediately after the originally-reported incident (client 9→10, ~290 lines under-delivered over ~41 min) — strengthens the case this is systemic, not a one-off, but wasn't isolated by a clean SIGKILL the way the first incident was; worth a final confirmation once D1-D4 are live.

C's shared-token fan-out design gives the phone an all-or-nothing trust boundary: it cannot be authorized for the Mac but not a specific server without new selective-auth UI, which this program does not build.

C's new POST /nodes endpoint is a fresh brute-force target for phoneToken guessing even with its own dedicated rate limiter (C6) — needs explicit abuse-testing before shipping, since it removes the natural throttle a full WS handshake per guess previously provided.

C12a-c's PWA rewrite touches nearly every function in a 1588-line file assuming a singular ws/state — mitigated by shipping the single-node regression guard (C12a) FIRST and isolated, and by the mandated findConv() helper + lint test (C12b), but this remains the highest regression-risk piece of workstream C.

No decoupled version-negotiation exists on the flightdeckd attach wire — D6's --supports-skip flag would break an older daemon's attach command outright if ever passed without A1's version gate; D6's brief makes this gate a hard precondition, not optional.

B9's 'no sudo at all' fallback behavior depends entirely on B6's fixture-D empirical finding (whether a --user systemd unit survives the bootstrap SSH session closing without linger) — this genuinely isn't known yet and must be determined before B9's brief can be finalized as written; B6 is scheduled to answer it first.

C1's cross-process config.json lock (flock-based) is a new mechanism this codebase has never needed before (flightdeckd has no analogue of tosse-code's SETTINGS_WRITE_LOCK) — needs careful review, and B10's run_init must remember to acquire the SAME lock when it shells out to `flightdeckd init` remotely, or the fix is incomplete.
